title: Constrained Estimation of Export and Import Inter‐Basin Groundwater Flows by Coupling Deep Learning With a Water‐Age Balance Approach
content:
Abstract

Inter-basin groundwater flow (IGF) is a critical process that links material and energy exchange between basins. Based on the source and flow direction of groundwater, IGF can be separated into export IGF and import IGF, which respectively denote the lateral outflow and inflow of groundwater from and into a basin. However, traditional hydrological modeling based on net IGF obscures the bidirectional exchange processes between basins. Furthermore, export and import IGF are difficult to measure directly, and existing methods to estimate them (e.g., hydrochemical tracing and groundwater modeling) are often costly and data-demanding. Therefore, this study innovatively proposes a method that integrates the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) with the ranked Storage Age Selection (rSAS) approach to partition export and import IGF. This method does not rely on detailed hydrogeological characterization and regional groundwater model. The feasibility of the proposed method was evaluated through a case study in the Lower Hafren basin, demonstrating its ability to quantify chloride transport processes within a unified water-age balance framework, allowing a constrained estimation of unobserved inter-basin groundwater flows. The results indicate that export and import IGF exhibit significantly different statistical characteristics compared to the net IGF. At the monthly timescale, the magnitudes of export IGF and import IGF are over two orders of magnitude greater than that of net IGF. And net IGF conceals the true seasonal fluctuation patterns inherent to export and import IGF. Furthermore, the uncertainties in the IGF partitioning were quantified and controlled through Bayesian uncertainty analysis and the LM-CMA-ES algorithm.
